subject: Docs updates for Regulated Workloads landing page (links + review checklist + publish timing)
body:
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, Jun 4, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Docs updates for Regulated Workloads landing page (links + review checklist + publish timing)

Team —

We’re close on the Regulated Workloads landing page PR (docs PR-421). Before we hit “publish,” I want to lock:

1) Cross-links: Security FAQ + Evidence Pack Index
2) Review checklist (copy + claims)
3) Timing for publishing + UTM/CTA

Proposed timeline:
- Today (6/4): incorporate final copy + link destinations
- Tomorrow (6/5): Security/PMM final pass
- Monday (6/9): merge
- Tuesday (6/10): publish + Marketing launches ads/outbound to the page

Asks:
- Soojin: can you confirm the “approved language” for the security section + footnote copy (esp. HIPAA phrasing) so Docs doesn’t guess?
- Naomi: can you sanity check the list of controls we name (SSO/SAML, audit logs, retention/residency, KMS/HSM) and any “do not say” items?
- Ben: confirm primary CTA (security review call vs benchmark download) + UTM convention.

Attachments:
- Regulated-Workloads-LandingPage-Copy-v7.docx
- Regulated-LandingPage-Review-Checklist-v2.pdf

If we can get thumbs-up by EOD tomorrow, we’re in good shape.

— Elliot
Elliot Price
Enterprise Docs
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 4, 2025 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Docs updates for Regulated Workloads landing page (links + review checklist + publish timing)

Yep — confirmed on language.

Key updates vs v6:
- Removed “HIPAA-ready” and anything that reads like a compliance certification.
- Use: “PHI-adjacent workflows” / “regulated and audit-driven environments.”
- Keep claims anchored to specific controls vs blanket statements.

Approved snippet for the security callout:
“Deploy with auditability and control: SSO/SAML, role-based access, encryption in transit/at rest, audit logs, configurable retention, and customer-managed keys (Dedicated/Private).”

Footnote guidance:
- Avoid “compliant with X” unless we’re specifically naming an attestation (e.g., SOC 2 report under NDA).

Drive link to latest copy (same as attachment but easier to comment):
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rD-regulated-copy-v7/view

Soojin


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 4, 2025 at 11:26 AM
Subject: Re: Docs updates for Regulated Workloads landing page (links + review checklist + publish timing)

Quick Security pass (high-level):

Good:
- “Controls-based” phrasing (audit logs, encryption, access control) is the right direction.
- Calling out Dedicated vs Private for customer-managed keys is accurate.

Edits / keepouts:
1) Don’t imply “data never stored” as a blanket statement. If you mention retention, say it’s “configurable” and point to policy/FAQ.
2) For SOC 2: OK to say “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA” (don’t say “certified”).
3) For HIPAA: do not say “HIPAA compliant / HIPAA-ready.” “PHI-adjacent” is fine.
4) For residency: avoid “guaranteed” unless you’re describing the deployment mode (Private in customer VPC/on-prem). “Supports data residency requirements via regional deployment options / Private deployments” is fine.

Cross-links I’d like on the page:
- Security FAQ (regulated buyers): sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/regulated-workloads-security-faq.json
- Evidence pack index (instructions + contents): sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/abm-pilot-security-evidence-pack-index.json

If you want, I can add 1–2 lines of “What’s in the evidence pack” as a short bulleted list, but we should keep it lightweight.

Naomi
Security & Compliance Product Alignment


---

From: Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 4, 2025 at 1:48 PM
Subject: Re: Docs updates for Regulated Workloads landing page (links + review checklist + publish timing)

On it.

Implementation plan for PR-421:
- Add a “Security & compliance” section with inline links:
  - “Read the Regulated Workloads Security FAQ”
  - “Request the security evidence pack (index)”
- Add a small “Deployment options” block that explicitly ties which controls are available where (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), without going too deep.
- Add the FAQ and evidence index as “next steps” resources below the main CTA (so they’re visible without making the page feel like a compliance portal).

Open questions:
1) CTA: do we want the primary CTA to route to “Talk to security” (form) or “Book a technical review” (Calendly-style)?
2) Any preference on naming in nav: “Regulated workloads” vs “Security-sensitive workloads”? (I lean regulated since that’s what the ABM pilot is using.)

If Ben confirms CTA + UTM needs today, I can update the PR and request final review tomorrow morning.

Kira
Technical Writer (Dedicated/Private)


---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 4, 2025 at 3:07 PM
Subject: Re: Docs updates for Regulated Workloads landing page (links + review checklist + publish timing)

Confirming CTA + tracking.

Primary CTA: “Request a security + architecture review” (goes to the existing regulated intake form; we’ll keep the questions short).
Secondary CTA: “Get the benchmark plan” (PDF download; gated).

UTM convention for the ABM pilot:
utm_campaign=abm_regulated_q2_2025
utm_source=linkedin | email | partner
utm_medium=paid_social | outbound | referral
utm_content=[ad_variant] or [sequence_touch]

Nav label: “Regulated workloads” is consistent with the ads + outbound sequences. +1 to not renaming right now.

Timing: If you can get it live by 6/10, we’ll point ads + sequences there starting 6/11.

Ben
Growth Marketing


---

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 5:41 PM
Subject: Re: Docs updates for Regulated Workloads landing page (links + review checklist + publish timing)

Thanks all — summarizing decisions + next steps.

Decisions:
- Primary CTA: “Request a security + architecture review” (form)
- Secondary CTA: “Get the benchmark plan” (gated)
- Keep nav label: “Regulated workloads”
- Cross-links on page: Security FAQ + Evidence Pack Index

Copy/claims guardrails (final):
- No “HIPAA-ready” / no “HIPAA compliant” language
- SOC 2: “Type II report available under NDA” only
- Residency: describe as “supported via regional options / Private deployments” (no blanket guarantees)
- Retention: “configurable retention” (avoid “no storage” claims)

Actions:
- Kira: please update PR-421 with link placements + the CTA buttons and request review from Naomi + Soojin.
- Naomi: final Security review on the PR tomorrow (6/6) by noon PT if possible.
- Soojin: final PMM copy pass on the PR tomorrow (same).
- Ben: send us the final form URL + benchmark asset ID once Marketing Ops has it.

If we get approvals tomorrow, we’ll merge Monday and publish Tuesday (6/10) as planned.

— Elliot
Elliot Price
Enterprise Docs
Redwood Inference
